searchText: `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Shanghai Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)` is described as: ```Description: Test sending ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 to request a Cancun payload: - Payload Attributes uses Shanghai timestamp - Payload Attributes' Beacon Root zero Verify that client returns INVALID_PARAMS_ERROR.``` but genesis config for this test starts cancun at 4661, and payload attrib timestamp is 0x1235 (4661) ergo a cancun timestamp, no? is this just wrong in the docs and is meant to say `Cancun timestamp`? `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Cancun Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)` is sending a non zero beacon root, so this test seems wrong. `Invalid PayloadAttributes: Missing BeaconRoot (Syncing) (Cancun) ` is also sending a non zero beacon root Ahh nice I think there a mismatch, I can update the comments and tweak the tests `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Shanghai Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)`: should be a sanity check for the usage of the fcuV2 method at Shanghai (not Cancun), verifying the appropriate response when the payloadAttributes are invalid for the fcuV2 -> calling the fcuV2 method with the beacon root field present within payloadAttributes at Shanghai. `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Cancun Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)`: Its the same as the above but at Cancun. fcuV2 with the beacon root field present in payloadAttributes Hence for both we expect an INVALID_PARAMS error `Invalid PayloadAttributes: Missing BeaconRoot (Syncing) (Cancun)`: this should be similar to the above, within the test we send a fcuV3 with `parentBeaconBlockRoot":null` and expect the response to be an INVALID_PARAMS error whilst syncing

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Shanghai Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)` is described as:

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content:
```Description:
Test sending ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 to request a Cancun payload:
- Payload Attributes uses Shanghai timestamp
- Payload Attributes' Beacon Root zero

Verify that client returns INVALID_PARAMS_ERROR.```

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: but genesis config for this test starts cancun at 4661, and payload attrib timestamp is 0x1235 (4661) ergo a cancun timestamp, no?

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: is this just wrong in the docs and is meant to say `Cancun timestamp`?

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Cancun Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)` is sending a non zero beacon root, so this test seems wrong.

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: `Invalid PayloadAttributes: Missing BeaconRoot (Syncing) (Cancun) ` is also sending a non zero beacon root

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content: Ahh nice I think there a mismatch, I can update the comments and tweak the tests

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content:
`ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Shanghai Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)`: should be a sanity check for the usage of the fcuV2 method at Shanghai (not Cancun), verifying the appropriate response when the payloadAttributes are invalid for the fcuV2 -> calling the fcuV2 method with the beacon root field present within payloadAttributes at Shanghai.

 `ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 To Request Cancun Payload, Zero Beacon Root (Cancun)`:  Its the same as the above but at Cancun. fcuV2 with the beacon root field present in payloadAttributes

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content: Hence for both we expect an INVALID_PARAMS error

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content: `Invalid PayloadAttributes: Missing BeaconRoot (Syncing) (Cancun)`: this should be similar to the above, within the test we send a fcuV3 with `parentBeaconBlockRoot":null` and expect the response to be an INVALID_PARAMS error whilst syncing
